A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RDBM study. Readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-I support reliable comparison despite reflow and removal of the appendix contents page.

before.justification: v1 reports original restoration, generalization, translation, and inpainting experiments, including quantitative comparisons, ablations, and appendix visual results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds measured memory use, inference time, and throughput in Appendix H.5 and Table S2.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 changes the t=T assignment from x_T=mu to x_{T-1}=mu, a limited revision to the specified sampling initialization. The residual modulation, bridge equations, training objective, and U-Net variants remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish an implementation change or rerun.

E1.justification: The five restoration tasks, real-world generalization datasets, POLED/TOLED evaluation, and translation/inpainting coverage are retained. Appendix Table S1 lists the same datasets. The added efficiency measurements use resolution settings within retained image coverage.

E2.justification: The same 13 restoration comparators and six translation/inpainting comparators remain evaluated. Table S2 reuses the restoration comparator set. Newly cited FLAIR and ResFusion are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: New Table S2 evaluates memory, inference time, and FPS at 256x256, 512x512, and 1024x1024. Existing dataset counts, restoration metrics, training budgets, model configurations, and stated 10-step testing setting are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix H.5 adds an analysis of how computational cost scales with image resolution across RDBM variants and comparators. Existing noise-schedule, lambda, sampling-step, and residual-choice ablations, noise-map analyses, and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new efficiency table likewise provides point estimates without introducing statistical reporting.

E6.justification: Table S2 adds computational results: for example, RDBM-L takes 0.504 seconds at 256x256 and 8.135 seconds at 1024x1024. Existing results in Tables 2-9 are unchanged, including RDBM-L's reported average PSNR/SSIM of 31.04/0.917 in Table 2.

T1.justification: Table 1 revises bridge specialization conditions, including VP lambda from infinity to 1/2 and Brownian bridge from lambda approaching 1/2 to 2*lambda*theta_t approaching 1. Appendix F.1 also changes the stated implied lambda from 1 to 1/2. The principal propositions and proofs remain.

C1.justification: The central claims of a unified bridge framework, residual-adaptive restoration, and superior empirical performance are retained. The revised conclusion explicitly mentions translation and inpainting, but these were already claimed and evaluated in v1.

C2.justification: New Appendix H.5 interprets RDBM as moderately efficient and balancing restoration performance against resource consumption. Existing explanations of sampling-step behavior and limitations concerning fixed lambda and distributions lacking correspondence remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix H.5 newly states the mixed dataset's 256-to-1024-pixel resolution range. Appendix I adds a claim that supplementary code is provided and public release will follow camera-ready submission, conflicting with the retained abstract statement that code is already public. Actual availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds four cited works: FLAIR, ResFusion, a pan-sharpening unfolded-network paper, and Universal Pansharpening Foundation Model. These modestly extend related-work coverage without changing the central positioning of RDBM.

P1.justification: v3 edits selected explanations and the conclusion, corrects 'Zero-Short' to 'Zero-Shot,' expands affiliations, adds acknowledgments, and removes the appendix contents page. Most prose and the main section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table S2, tightens figure/table spacing, and corrects Figure 7's caption from TOLED generalization to image translation and inpainting. Existing empirical image panels and table structures are largely retained.

improvement.justification: Table S2 usefully supplements v1's parameter/FLOP counts with measured memory and runtime across resolutions. Specific bridge-parameter corrections and the corrected Figure 7 caption also improve clarity. These are limited gains with unchanged restoration evidence; sparse efficiency-measurement details and contradictory code-release wording constrain the reproducibility benefit.
